transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 mins
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (Summit CISO), Laura Chen (Security PM), Tom Gallagher (Infra Lead), Aisha Patel (Compliance)

Summary: Quick posture readout for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 alignment, discuss Trust Center access + evidence handoff, RBAC/SSO mapping, audit logs retention and region/data residency for EU workloads. Agreed next: share Trust Center link, redacted SOC2, schedule infra deep dive + POC kickoff.

Topics: Trust Center & reports, controls mapping, RBAC and SSO (SAML/Okta), audit log collection/retention, KMS/encryption at rest, data residency and region routing, evidence handoff process.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; uh we wanted to give a quick posture walk through and make sure we cover the Trust Center access plus nitty grit of evidence flow. I'm Jordan from Redwood AE.
[00:22] Mark: Thanks Jordan. I'm Mark, CISO at Summit. We're in the middle of scoping our SOC 2 and want to confirm how Redwood can fit with our EU data boundary requirements and how we verify logs.
[01:05] Priya: Hey, Priya here. I'll take the technical pieces — RBAC, KMS, log forwarding. Quick note, some of the docs we have in the Trust Center are read-only links we can grant; also the SOC 2 PDF we can provide redacted version for initial review.
[01:40] Laura: That would be great. Our auditors usually want the control narratives and a bit of evidence around key controls — SSO configs, user provisioning, and audit logs.
[02:10] Tom: From infra, I'm mostly concerned about latency and the residency routing — we can't have certain PII leave EU region for legal reasons. Is that supported with Redwood Dedicated or Private?
[02:40] Priya: Good question. We support dedicated capacity you can pin to region, and Private (VPC / on-prem) for stricter needs. For hosted, we have regional endpoints, but the rule of thumb is for EU-only workloads you should look at Dedicated or Private — however we do have org-level routing policies so requests from EU can hit EU variants. There's also the option to configure model variants so sensitive traffic stays in EU.
[03:15] Mark: When you say "regional endpoints" does that also mean logs and audit trails stay in-region, or are they centralized in Redwood's US control plane?
[03:40] Jordan: Historically the control plane metadata is in our control plane, but we have options — for Private deployments the control plane can be within customer's VPC; for Dedicated we offer data residency controls and log routing. We'll send the exact mapping doc.
[04:05] Aisha: Auditors ask for log retention policy and evidence that logs are immutable. How do you handle tamper-evident logs / chain of custody?
[04:30] Priya: We ship logs to the customer's destination: S3, BigQuery, or syslog. For immutability you can leverage object lock on S3 or your SIEM's append-only settings. We also publish an audit events spec — e.g., user auth events, admin actions, model change events — that auditors use for mapping.
[05:08] Mark: Does Redwood integrate with our KMS? We run AWS KMS with key policies and want envelope encryption so Redwood can't decrypt customer data.
[05:35] Priya: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. For hosted customers we support bring-your-own-key via Customer Master Key (CMK) and envelope encryption. The flow is: model inference payload gets encrypted with ephemeral data key encrypted by your KMS — we only see the ciphertext. We'll share an example diagram.
[06:00] Tom: Are there any performance tradeoffs with envelope keys? Latency implications?
[06:20] Priya: Minimal. We cache the DEKs per request window to avoid round-trip to KMS for every token. There's a small crypto overhead on key rotation windows. We'll show metrics in the infra deep dive.
[06:50] Jordan: Quick pause — two asks: 1) we'll provide the Trust Center link + SOC 2 redacted; 2) Priya will run a KMS and RBAC demo with Tom next week.
[07:12] Laura: Sounds good. Also interested in control mapping: which of your controls map to CC6/CC7 (change mgmt), CC8 (access). Do you have a controls matrix?
[07:40] Jordan: Yes, we have a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 CC criteria and ISO clauses. I'll attach. Note sometimes the wording isn't an exact one-to-one, but it's a good starting point.
[08:05] Mark: For evidence handoff, we prefer a secure transfer—S3 presigned or internal vault access. What's your recommended flow?
[08:30] Priya: Typical pattern: we drop evidence artifacts to a customer-owned S3 bucket (via cross-account role) or provide read-only Trust Center access. For ad-hoc artifacts we can do presigned links with expiration.
[09:00] Tom: Can you show an example of RBAC roles? We use okta groups and SCIM for provisioning. We want least privilege: separate admin, infra, model-deploy roles.
[09:30] Priya: Yep. Our standard roles: admin (org-wide), model-deploy, viewer, billing. We support SAML + SCIM for group sync. We'll show a user flow: Okta -> SCIM -> groups -> mapped roles in Redwood. Minor caveat, sometimes SCIM attr mapping needs a tweak for groups with nested membership.
[10:00] Mark: How are API tokens audited? We need to show token issuance, rotations, and revocations.
[10:22] Priya: API tokens are logged with issuance events, and admins can list and revoke tokens. We store token hashes (so we never show raw token), and rotation policy can be enforced via RBAC. The audit event includes actor, scope, and IP.
[11:00] Jordan: Quick note on the Trust Center itself — it contains SOC 2 Type II report, pen test summary, certs, and a controls mapping XSL. We'll give you read access and we can whitebox any sections you need.
[11:30] Laura: Great. Auditors sometimes want to see the change window — meaning how model versions are rolled out and how rollback is handled. Any write-up?
[11:55] Priya: We have a rollouts doc describing canary deploys, A/B, automatic fallback to earlier model variant; all of which are recorded in deployment audit events. Some product names occasionally get transcribed oddly in notes (like 'Redwood Pivot' — that's me mis-saying 'Redwood Private') — ignore that in the doc.
[12:25] Mark: (laughs) noted. Also need to understand encryption at rest for the model artifacts — where are the model weights stored and are they encrypted?
[12:50] Priya: Model artifacts are stored encrypted at rest; for Dedicated and Private deployments it can be customer-managed storage. For hosted artifacts, we use customer-specific bucket with server-side encryption.
[13:20] Tom: If we want to keep the KV cache local to EU, is that an option? We can't have cached tokenized context cross-region.
[13:45] Priya: Yes, KV cache placement is part of deployment config. For EU-only workloads the cache and inference nodes are pinned to EU region. I did want to call out — sometimes people say 'KV cash' in notes, but it's 'KV cache' — small transcription joke.
[14:10] Aisha: Regarding retention, our policy is 7 years for certain records, but for ephemeral logs we want 1 year. Can you customize retention per stream?
[14:35] Priya: You can set retention on the destination side. For example, S3 lifecycle rules or BigQuery dataset retention. We can also configure the event types we forward — so you might only keep admin and auth events long-term.
[15:05] Mark: On the subject of evidence automation: will Redwood push continuous evidence or is it manual snapshot?
[15:30] Jordan: We can do both. For instance, continuous audit events go to your SIEM (streaming), and periodic snapshots (control evidence bundles) can be delivered weekly to your S3. We also support an audit portal (Trust Center) where you can download zipped bundles.
[16:00] Tom: Do you keep configuration history for RBAC role changes? Our auditors want changes with diffs and who approved.
[16:25] Priya: Yes, role changes are stored as part of config history with before/after diffs, actor, and timestamp. We can surface the diff as part of evidence bundles.
[17:00] Mark: Any known gaps for ISO 27001 specifically? We wanted to know if you have statement of applicability and control evidence for Annex A items.
[17:30] Jordan: We maintain an ISO mapping doc and SoA. For some infra-specific Annex A clauses we rely on cloud provider attestations — we map that in the evidence. If you have a particular annex item you want us to expand on, say A.9 (access control) or A.10 (cryptography), tell us and we'll pull artifacts.
[18:05] Laura: We'll take A.9 and A.10 first. Also curious about separation of duties — do you partition operator access between infra and app?
[18:30] Priya: We have distinct role groups and policy bounding; operator sequences are recorded in audit trails for separation enforcement.
[19:05] Tom: For SSO, do you support multiple identity providers per org (e.g., Okta for engineering, Azure AD for business)?
[19:30] Priya: We do allow multiple IdPs via aliasing, but the group mapping must be consolidated so roles are consistent. SCIM sync can be configured per IdP. There are edge cases for email-normalization that we've seen — we'll include the gotchas doc.
[20:10] Jordan: Quick check — auditors sometimes request raw logs for a time window. Do we provide?
[20:30] Priya: We provide archived logs per request via your S3 export for a time window; ad-hoc delivery is supported but we recommend setting up continuous export for compliance.
[21:05] Mark: Any SLA commitments for Dedicated around uptime and forensic access?
[21:30] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and prioritized support. For forensics we can expedite evidence pulls. Specific SLA language we'll share in the contract addendum.
[22:00] Aisha: About proof of key custody — auditors want to see KMS policy and rotation cadence. Can you share a template policy?
[22:25] Priya: We'll share a sample key policy and rotation schedule. For private deployments you can host the key; for dedicated we support CMK with policy binding.
[23:00] Tom: I'm concerned about data spillage in logs — e.g., prompt text with PII. Do you provide redaction or scrubbers?
[23:30] Priya: We have redaction hooks and heuristics — you can enable PII scrubbers pre-ingest; for hosted customers we also provide a redact-on-ingest pipeline. However be aware heuristics are not perfect; best to keep high-sensitivity workloads on Private or Dedicated and encrypt payloads client-side.
[24:10] Mark: On cost: is there extra for dedicated routing & region pinning?
[24:35] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated/residency has committed capacity pricing. We'll include pricing examples in the follow up.
[25:00] Laura: Can we get a sample evidence bundle for one control so auditors can see format?
[25:20] Jordan: Yes; we'll drop a sample zipped bundle (anonymized) in the Trust Center.
[25:50] Priya: Also want to mention model change evidence — when a model is updated we capture model ID, change log, who promoted and timestamp — that's included in the deployment audit trail.
[26:30] Tom: For the POC, we'd like to run a restricted traffic slice: EU-only inference, SAML SSO, KMS CMK, and logs to our S3 — minimal dataset. How long to stand that up?
[26:55] Priya: Roughly 2-3 weeks for config & infra if all approvals move quick; if you're using Private it could take longer. For Dedicated it depends on capacity queue but typically 1-2 weeks once committed.
[27:30] Laura: Our timeline — auditors want evidence in 8 weeks. So we need a plan fast.
[27:50] Jordan: Let's target POC kickoff week of 2026-05-25 and a mid-POC check around 2026-06-08. We'll align milestones with your auditor needs.
[28:20] Mark: Any reference customers with similar regulatory profile (insurance)?
[28:40] Jordan: We have a couple in financial services and insurance — we'll share redacted reference list. Note sometimes the transcriber mangles names — apologies in advance.
[29:05] Aisha: On evidence access control: can we limit Trust Center access by role so auditors only see certain docs?
[29:30] Priya: Yes, Trust Center access is RBAC gated; you can create auditor-level roles with read-only scope. We can also create expiring invites.
[30:00] Tom: A small technical ask — when you forward logs, do you include request bodies or just metadata?
[30:20] Priya: By default we forward metadata and audit events; request bodies are redacted unless you opt-in. For PII-sensitive workloads you'd keep bodies encrypted client-side.
[31:00] Mark: Let's cover the evidence handoff cadence — weekly snapshots vs on-demand.
[31:20] Jordan: Weekly snapshots are common; auditors like that because it gives a deterministic window. On-demand exports are available for ad-hoc deep dives.
[32:00] Laura: If we need custom control evidence, who owns creating the artifact? Do you create screenshots or do we?
[32:25] Priya: We can create system-generated artifacts: configs export, logs, and screenshots for UI configurations — but some artifacts (internal policies) must come from you. We can help with templating.
[33:00] Tom: Ok, let's talk KMS flow again — can you summarize the envelope flow briefly?
[33:20] Priya: Sure: 1) Client encrypts payload with ephemeral DEK, 2) DEK encrypted with customer CMK in KMS, 3) encrypted DEK and payload sent to Redwood, 4) inference executed with ciphertext — Redwood never has plaintext keys. For inference that require plaintext inside the runtime you can use Private deployment where decryption happens inside your VPC under your KMS. We'll add diagrams.
[34:10] Mark: Anything else on SAML/SCIM gotchas?
[34:30] Priya: Timeouts for SCIM jobs, nested groups, and attribute mapping differences (mail vs userPrincipalName) are common. We'll include a checklist.
[35:05] Jordan: Quick commercial note — Dedicated commitments influence lead time for capacity. We'll include an estimated timeline in follow-up.
[35:35] Laura: For auditors, evidence traceability is key — can you provide a packaged chain of custody?
[36:00] Priya: Yes, our evidence bundles include a manifest with hashes and timestamps. If you need NFT style chain-of-custody we can sign with our key and provide verification steps.
[36:40] Tom: On-hosted vs dedicated: for isolation, what about PCI-level isolation?
[37:00] Jordan: For PCI we recommend Private or strict Dedicated with dedicated tenancy. We'll loop in security to map PCI controls.
[37:30] Aisha: Any automation for control testing? Like continuous control monitoring?
[37:55] Priya: We have some continuous checks (uptime, config drift) and can push alerts; full continuous control testing depends on the control and sometimes requires customer side probes.
[38:30] Mark: What about log integrity? Any signing of events?
[38:50] Priya: We can sign events and store signatures alongside logs. For high-assurance customers we support an append-only ledger export.
[39:30] Jordan: We'll add that as an optional architecture for high-assurance POCs.
[40:00] Laura: Let's confirm the next concrete steps: trust center link, redacted SOC2, KMS diagram, controls matrix, schedule infra deep-dive.
[40:20] Jordan: Correct — we'll send in next 3 business days.
[40:40] Tom: For the deep-dive can we have sample endpoints we can hit? strober? (muttered)
[41:00] Priya: We'll provide staging endpoints and a runbook; note staging sometimes has different perf char so it's for functional verification not final perf numbers.
[41:30] Mark: Anything regarding retention for legal hold? We occasionally need indefinite preserves for litigation.
[41:50] Priya: Legal hold support comes via your storage bucket settings (S3 Object Lock governance) — we can coordinate with your infra folks.
[42:20] Aisha: For audit evidence access we prefer a single zipped package per audit period. Is that supported?
[42:45] Jordan: Yes, weekly or monthly bundles are supported.
[43:10] Tom: If we do a POC and are happy, how quickly can we transition to production?
[43:30] Jordan: Depends on deployment mode — Dedicated to prod often takes 2-4 weeks after POC sign-off; Private depends on your internal procurement and on-prem setup. We'll include migration checklist.
[44:00] Laura: Any standard redaction templates you provide for SOC2?
[44:20] Priya: We'll include a redaction checklist and sample redacted SOC2.
[44:50] Mark: Regarding the controls mapping doc — can you show a sample row?
[45:10] Jordan: Sure: e.g., Access control: Redwood policy (RBAC) -> SOC 2 CC6 -> Evidence: RBAC config export + audit events + SCIM logs. We'll attach that.
[45:40] Tom: Ok let's cement dates: Trust Center + SOC2 by 2026-05-18, POC kickoff week of 2026-05-25, infra deep-dive 2026-05-20.
[46:05] Jordan: Sounds good — priya will send calendar invites.
[46:30] Aisha: Two small compliance asks: redaction proof for one sample and a KMS policy template.
[46:50] Priya: We'll add to deliverables.
[47:20] Mark: Any blockers from your side for the short timeline?
[47:40] Jordan: Nothing major — availability of Dedicated capacity is the main variable, but for POC we can use staging or Private depending on your preference.
[48:10] Tom: If we want guaranteed EU data residency for production, we need a contract clause.
[48:30] Jordan: Right, residency and data processing addenda are contractual items. We'll route that to legal and include in the proposal.
[49:00] Laura: Ok final question — do you have SOC 2 on a rolling 12 month or annual?
[49:20] Jordan: Our SOC 2 Type II is annual with a 12 month coverage period. The report we share will show coverage dates.
[49:50] Mark: Great. Anything else from Redwood?
[50:05] Priya: Nothing more from me— we'll prep the infra deep-dive materials.
[50:20] Jordan: Thanks everyone. Quick recap of who does what and due dates.
[50:40] Laura: Thanks all.
[51:00] Mark: Appreciate it.
[51:20] Tom: Bye.
[51:35] Jordan: End call — follow-up notes to be sent.

--- End of transcript ---
